scientific_integrity: The claim is proved symbolically from the Euclid--Euler form of even perfect numbers, exact odd-part factorization, and a complete modulo-8 argument. The included program only regression-checks the residue calculation and is not used as an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem covers exponents m>=5 congruent to 1 modulo 4. It does not treat exponents congruent to 3 modulo 4 beyond the already-known cubic case, so the full conjecture remains open.
title: No even perfect number is a sum of two positive \(m\)-th powers when \(m\equiv1\pmod4\)
